## v0.3.0

### Breaking Changes

**Table resize API — encapsulated `ResizeState`/`ResizeEvent`** (#11)
- `Table::resize` no longer takes four separate callbacks (`on_resize_start`, `on_resize`, `on_resize_end`, `widths`); callers now pass a single `(state: &ResizeState, on_event: impl Fn(ResizeEvent) -> Message)` pair
- `ResizeState::new(widths)` holds both the column widths and drag bookkeeping in one value; configure per-column clamps with `.min_width(f32)` (default 40.0) and `.max_width(f32)` (default unbounded)
- Read column widths in `view` via `state.resize.width(col_index)`
- In `update`, a single `state.resize.apply(event)` replaces the previous three-branch match

#### Migration

Before:
```rust
table()
    .on_resize_start(|i| Message::ResizeStart(i))
    .on_resize(|i, w| Message::Resize(i, w))
    .on_resize_end(Message::ResizeEnd)
    .widths(&self.col_widths)
```

After:
```rust
table()
    .resize(&self.resize, Message::Resize)
```

And in update:
```rust
Message::Resize(event) => { self.resize.apply(event); }
```
